title: Photon-Number Discrimination from Increasing Time-of-Arrival Separation in Wide Superconducting Microstrip Single-Photon Detectors
authors: Hsin-Yeh Wu, Shu-Xiao Liu, Boris Tuchming, Xavier-François Navick, Pu-Kai Wang, Yi-Ren Wu, Jia-Wern Chen, Marc Besançon, Jean-François Glicenstein, Pisin Chen, Yu-Jung Lu, Stathes Paganis
abstract: Measurements of photon-number-dependent time-of-arrival (TOA) distributions in wide NbN superconducting microstrip single-photon detectors (SMSPDs) are presented. Two \SI{10}{\um}-long devices with widths of \SI{3.2}{\um} and \SI{6.4}{\um} are characterized under pulsed \SI{515}{nm} excitation. The TOA histograms are described by sums of exponentially modified Gaussian (EMG) components, with the wider device exhibiting components assigned to photon numbers up to \(n=8\). Adjacent TOA peaks become more distinguishable relative to their widths at higher photon number, in contrast to the compression of neighboring photon-number timing shifts observed in conventional narrow-wire SNSPDs. For the components assigned to \(n=7\) and \(n=8\), the FWHM-normalized peak separation is \(2.15\), and the fitted EMG distributions yield an equal-prior pairwise TOA-assignment fidelity of \(99.6\%\). The EMG exponential-tail parameter \(τ_n\) decreases strongly with photon number, while the Gaussian-location parameter \(μ_n\) continues to shift between neighboring components. A phenomenological model motivated by absorption-site-dependent vortex processes and collective current redistribution captures these timing trends. These results support wide SMSPDs as a platform for TOA-based photon-number discrimination at high photon number, relevant to multiphoton-state characterization and photonic quantum information processing. The same geometry also provides a setting to examine how the spatial distribution of photon absorption affects vortex-assisted detection.
summary: This work demonstrates that wide superconducting microstrip single-photon detectors can resolve distinct time-of-arrival signatures corresponding to high photon numbers (up to $n=8$). By analyzing the detailed shape of the TOA histograms using advanced fitting techniques, the authors confirm that these detectors are a viable platform for advanced photon-number discrimination crucial for quantum information processing.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of achieving high photon-number discrimination (PND) in superconducting single-photon detectors.
main_result: Wide superconducting microstrip detectors show improved and distinguishable time-of-arrival (TOA) peaks up to $n=8$, confirming their potential for high-photon-number quantum state characterization.
method: The authors characterized detectors by measuring TOA histograms under pulsed excitation and fitting them using sums of Exponentially Modified Gaussian (EMG) components.
model_or_system: The physical system is a wide NbN superconducting microstrip single-photon detector (SMSPD). The detection process is modeled phenomenologically based on absorption-site-dependent vortex nucleation and subsequent current redistribution.
key_observables: Time-of-Arrival (TOA) histograms, EMG parameters ($\mu_n, \sigma_n, 	au_n$), FWHM-normalized peak separation, and equal-prior pairwise TOA-assignment fidelity.
important_parameters: Photon number ($n$), detector width (3.2 $\mu$m and 6.4 $\mu$m), and the exponential-tail parameter $	au_n$ which decreases strongly with $n$.
main_assumptions: The timing trends are modeled using a phenomenological approach motivated by vortex processes, and the analysis assumes the TOA can be decomposed into nucleation and traversal contributions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the edge-sensitive nucleation and vortex-traversal process, and show the photon-number dependence of TOA separation and assignment fidelity, confirming increasing distinguishability with $n$.
paper_structure: The paper presents measurements on wide SMSPDs, analyzes the TOA histograms via EMG fitting, develops a phenomenological model linking timing shifts to vortex dynamics, and concludes by validating the platform for high-photon-number PND.
why_interesting: The ability to resolve distinct timing signatures for multiple photons ($n=8$) directly relates to the fundamental requirements for quantum state tomography and the characterization of multi-photon quantum states.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic illustration of the edge-sensitive nucleation and subsequent vortex-traversal processes considered in the timing description. (a) Bias current ﬂows uniformly in the superconducting microstrip before photon absorption. (b) Absorbed photons generate localized hotspots and redistribute the current density. (c) A vortex nucleates stochastically at the strip edge, with the relevant transverse coordinate set by the edge-nearest hotspot, ˜xmin. (d) The vortex then traverses the strip, producing the dissipative event associated with the electrical readout pulse.

FIG. 2. Representative stacked TOA histograms for (a) Device A and (b) Device B, with EMG decomposition overlays. Three representative incident optical powers are shown in each panel, increasing from bottom to top. The annotations give the incident optical power P and the ﬁtted Poisson mean ⟨n⟩ﬁt, obtained from the Poisson description of the ﬁtted component areas. Device A is shown on a linear scale, whereas Device B is shown on a logarithmic scale to display its broader dynamic range. Colored curves show the individual EMG components, labeled by n, and the red curves show the total ﬁts, including a constant background term. Peaks are resolved through n = 5 for Device A and through n = 8...
